what_it_does: Estimating how much power a chip design will consume is critical early in the design process, but collecting enough example measurements from different configurations to train a machine-learning predictor is expensive and time-consuming when the chip does not yet exist. AutoPower tackles this by recognizing that total chip power is not one big lump — it is the sum of nearly independent components (clock distribution, on-chip static memory called SRAM, logic gates, and so on). By building a separate, small prediction model for each component and using structural information visible at the architecture planning stage, the system needs very few real measurements to reach accurate predictions. This few-shot approach (learning from only a handful of examples) makes power estimation practical at very early design stages.
